answer: The challenge noted regarding holding private actors responsible for AI existential risks under international human rights law is that the current legal framework places obligations solely on state actors, reflecting a vertical relationship between the citizen and the state. As a result, private actors are not under any legal obligation to take precautions to address AI as an existential threat. While there is some movement toward recognizing private actors being subjected to human rights obligations, this has not yet emerged as a matter of international law. Therefore, international human rights law does not fully capture the modern realities of power given the significant role private corporations play in the development of AI.
